transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-19
- Time: 10:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Lena (NovaPay Eng Lead), Omar (NovaPay SRE), Priya (NovaPay PM)

Summary: quick weekly check-in on the throughput POC, focus on continuous batching, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure, and next benchmark steps.

Topics: continuous batching behavior; how concurrency interacts with batching; queue thresholds and retry/backpressure; KV/prefix cache warmup; p95/p99 latency targets; traffic shaping to match production.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick roll call — we have Maya and Carlos from Redwood, Lena, Omar, Priya from NovaPay?
00:08 Lena: yep that's us, hi Maya, hi Carlos
00:10 Carlos: great, quick agenda, we'll go over last week's throughput runs, call out what we changed, and propose a tuning pass then outline next benchmark runs
00:20 Omar: quick note — we noticed a weird tail at p99 last run, like spikes when concurrency hit about 120, curious if that's queuing on the Redwood side or our client side
00:32 Maya: good, yeah that's exactly what we'll dig into. Carlos do you want to start with the run summary?
00:36 Carlos: sure, so last run we did sustained 10k rps emulation, client side sim with 100 concurrency threads, we saw average token throughput looking good, p50 ~ 40ms token, p95 around 180ms, p99 was jumping 800ms to 1.2s in bursts. We had continuous batching enabled with batch size cap at 256 and a batching window of 20ms, but because concurrency varied batches sometimes collapsed into smaller sizes which increased token overhead
01:05 Lena: when you say collapsed you mean smaller batches hit the model more frequently?
01:08 Carlos: exactly, so instead of a full 200+ token batch we had a lot of 20-50 token batches. That increases per-token overhead and memory churn. Also, we saw KV cache misses during the initial part of the run which increased latency for first few requests in a sequence
01:25 Omar: is that KV as in key-value cache in the runtime, or some client cache?
01:28 Carlos: that's runtime KV cache — our LM serving keeps a KV cache across tokens for incremental decoding. Warmup was slower because sequences weren't pipelined consistently.
01:36 Priya: do we think this is a config issue or workload mismatch? Our traffic in prod has a lot of short requests interspersed with longer chats, so maybe the synthetic profile isn't matching
01:47 Carlos: good point — the shape of traffic hugely impacts batching. If you have many short requests at random intervals batching window will flush more often. We recommended two options: increase batching window to 40-60ms to allow more accumulation, or use an adaptive window with concurrency-based heuristics. There's tradeoff: larger window increases latency floor but improves throughput/cost
02:12 Lena: our SLO is p95 < 250ms, p99 < 800ms for chat latency end-to-end. We want to stay under that while maximizing throughput/cost efficiency
02:22 Maya: ok that's helpful. Right now your p95 was ~180 so still within, p99 is the issue. For p99 we usually tune queue depth and implement backpressure so the system rejects or delays to keep tail latency bounded. Carlos, can you explain the queueing approach?
02:37 Carlos: yeah so we have a request queue per worker shard. We set a queue size threshold and a concurrency cap per GPU. When queue length exceeds threshold we either start shedding (rejecting non-critical requests) or trigger the overload policy which routes to a lower-cost/latency-optimized model variant or region. Also, we can prioritize warm sequences to hit KV cache first. In your runs we didn't enable request prioritization so cold sequences got mixed in and caused more KV misses
03:05 Omar: that sounds ... reasonable. On NovaPay side we have a client-side concurrency limiter so we thought we'd be protected, turns out in the last run that limiter was accidentally left at default and the client ended up spiking concurrency. We'll confirm before the next run
03:18 Lena: also curious about Dedicated burst capacity you mentioned in the doc; would that help smooth p99s?
03:23 Maya: Dedicated burst gives you reserved GPU pools and the option for extra burst nodes to absorb spikes. It helps if your peaks are unpredictable. But it's more about capacity; you'll still need queueing and prioritization to control tail latency. There's also hybrid routing — host critical traffic on dedicated, non-critical on hosted cheaper endpoints
03:43 Priya: any gotchas with quantization or kernel selection affecting throughput? We saw a small perf delta on different model variants
03:50 Carlos: yes, kernel selection and quantization affect throughput/latency. For high throughput we prefer quantized model with optimized kernels for the target GPU, but it can increase p99 variance if numerical paths behave differently on short vs long sequences. We suggested trying q4_0 for this workload; it's a good balance. Also, make sure your sequence length cap is aligned with model config — long sequences blow up memory and reduce effective batch sizes
04:18 Maya: noted. Ok let's talk concrete tuning steps. Carlos?
04:22 Carlos: propose we push three changes for the next two runs: 1) increase batching window to 45ms and raise batch size cap to 384, 2) set worker queue threshold to 400 requests and concurrency cap per GPU at 110, 3) enable request prioritization for sequences flagged as warm (we'll provide a header to your client to mark warm continuation requests).
04:46 Lena: raising concurrency cap? last time p99 spiked near 120 — will 110 avoid spikes?
04:51 Carlos: yes the cap at 110 is conservative; it avoids saturating internal scheduling. The client concurrency limiter should be set to match — Carlos (SE) will provide the exact client-side parameter to set. If you need more overall throughput we'll scale nodes horizontally rather than pushing single GPU harder
05:06 Omar: what about batching window — 45ms sounds like it might add 20-30ms to p50; are we ok with that?
05:11 Maya: yes but it's a tradeoff — you gain throughput and reduce p99. With 45ms window you might see p50 increase slightly but p95 remains similar or better; we will measure.
05:21 Priya: for the benchmark shape, can we run two sustained runs 20 minutes each, one emulating daytime traffic and one with spiky short requests to stress tail?
05:29 Carlos: absolutely, recommended. Also please capture detailed traces and the worker-side throughput logs so we can correlate queue depth to latency spikes. We'll share a Grafana dashboard link and the log ingest instructions
05:40 Maya: action items recap: Carlos to share tuned config and load scripts; Omar to upload logs and confirm client limiter setting; Maya to send pricing for burst capacity; Lena to run the two benchmark shapes and confirm results; meet next Thursday to review.
05:56 Omar: quick question about fallback routing — you mentioned routing to lower-cost model variants, is that seamless?
06:01 Carlos: yes we can route by policy; for example at high queue depth we fall back from the full 7B model to a trimmed 3B variant that preserves latency but slightly different quality. We keep a compatibility mapping so API responses maintain the same schema, but quality tradeoffs can require product-level acceptance
06:23 Lena: will that require client changes?
06:26 Carlos: no client changes if you trust our routing policy; otherwise we can expose a header instructing client when a fallback occurred for audit purposes
06:34 Priya: can we get an estimate of cost impact if we increase batching window vs add horizontal nodes?
06:39 Maya: yes I'll put together a quick delta in the pricing doc. Generally increasing batching window reduces per-token cost, adding nodes increases fixed cost but reduces latency variance
06:51 Carlos: one more technical note: the KV cache warmup — for chat continuations we recommend either pinning conversations to a worker for warm cache locality or using our prefix caching to prepopulate common prompts. We'll include config for both approaches
07:05 Omar: we'll try pinning on the first run to see effect, then compare with prefix cache enabled on second run
07:11 Lena: timeline on logs — Omar will push logs today, we should get tuned config by Wednesday?
07:15 Carlos: yes I'll share config and the load generator script by end of day Wednesday, or earlier if possible
07:21 Maya: perfect. Any other blockers?
07:24 Priya: just one — security asked for the audit log format for routing decisions; could you send that?
07:29 Maya: yep we'll include a short document with SAML/SSO and audit log examples, and the SOC2 excerpts — but full security pack we'll send to your security team via the secure portal
07:40 Lena: ok thanks all, let's reconvene once we have the runs done and logs analyzed
07:45 Maya: thanks everyone, meeting adjourned

Notes about transcription quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "batching window" transcribed as "bashing window" in one segment), speaker labels are accurate but may be slightly fuzzy in places.
